newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Chretien maintains economic team.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Chretien maintains economic team.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien shuffled his cabinet on Wednesday but maintained his overall economic direction with the reappointment of tight-fisted Paul Martin as finance minister.

"The economic team is totally unchanged," Chretien spokesman Peter Donolo said. "I think it's a very strong message about direction, about continuity, about seeing through the (deficit reduction) plan."

In another sign that Chretien would stay the fiscal course of slashing Canada's budget deficit, he relieved left-leaning Heritage Minister Sheila Copps of her additional role as deputy prime minister. Former government house leader Herb Gray succeeded her as deputy prime minister.

Chretien reappointed John Manley, regarded with Martin as as fiscal conservative, as industry minister. Justice Minister Allan Rock was moved to the health portfolio, one that Copps had reportedly sought amid improving prospects for a budget surplus in coming years.

Environment Minister Sergio Marchi became international trade minister, replacing Art Eggleton, who moved into the sensitive defense portfolio, succeeding the acerbic Doug Young, who was defeated in the June 2 election.

Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy, more open than some to the idea of taking human rights into account, stayed in his post. Anne McLellan, who narrowly won re-election in conservative Alberta, was named justice minister, perhaps sign+aling a less activist approach to justice and social issues.
